issues.failure_explanation: In estimating $R_{12}$, the third term contains an absolute value inside the expectation: $\hat{\mathbb{E}}[|\partial_t \omega(x + h^{1/2} X) - \partial_t \omega(x)|]$. The first-order Taylor expansion term is $\langle \partial_t D_x \omega, h^{1/2} X \rangle$, which is of order $h^{1/2}$. The proof drops this term by asserting that $X$ is zero-mean without mean uncertainty. However, the expectation of the absolute value $\hat{\mathbb{E}}[|\langle \partial_t D_x \omega, h^{1/2} X \rangle + O(h)|]$ does not vanish and is strictly of order $h^{1/2}$, not $h$. Zero mean does not imply that absolute moments vanish.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the first-order term in $R_{12}$ bounded by $h^{1/2} \|\partial_t D_x \omega\|_\infty M_{X_1}^1$, add this term to the consistency error bound in Lemma 3.2, and adjust the constant in front of $\varepsilon^{-2} h^{1/2}$ in $E_1(\varepsilon, h)$ and $E_2(\varepsilon, h)$.
issues.overall_effect: The bound on $R_1$ in Lemma 3.2 is missing a term of order $h^{1/2} \|\partial_t D_x \omega\|_\infty M_{X_1}^1$. When applied to the mollified solution $u^\varepsilon$ (or $u_h^\varepsilon$), this term contributes an error of order $h^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-2}$, which has the exact same scaling as the existing $h^{1/2} \|D_x^3 \omega\|_\infty$ term in $E_1$ and $E_2$.
issues.title: Invalid cancellation of first-order spatial Taylor term inside absolute expectation in time consistency estimate
issues.why_classification: The omitted term scales as $h^{1/2} \varepsilon^{-2}$ upon mollification, which matches an existing leading error term already present in $E_1$ and $E_2$. Absorbing it requires only a routine local adjustment of constants and preserves all rates, exponents, and theorem statements without any loss of scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof sets $q_1 = 3/2$ and interpolates between the bounds $|\Delta_x \omega| \le 2\|D_x \omega\|_\infty$ and $|\Delta_x \omega| \le \|D_{xz}^2 \omega\|_\infty h^{1/\alpha} |Z|$ using weights $q_1 - \delta$ and $\delta$. However, Assumption 2.5(v) allows any $\delta \in (\frac{3}{4}\alpha \vee 1, \alpha)$. For $\alpha \in (1.5, 2)$, one may choose $\delta \in (1.5, \alpha)$, which implies $q_1 - \delta < 0$. When the exponent $q_1 - \delta$ is negative, the pointwise inequality fails for small $|Z|$ because $(h^{1/\alpha} |Z|)^{q_1 - \delta} \to \infty$ as $|Z| \to 0$. Consequently, the integral cannot be bounded by $\tilde{\mathbb{E}}[|Z|^\delta]$ whenever $\delta > 3/2$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the range of $\delta$ in Assumption 2.5(v) to $\delta \in (\frac{3}{4}\alpha \vee 1, \alpha \wedge \frac{3}{2}]$, ensuring $q_1 - \delta \ge 0$, and adjust the supremum over $\delta$ and resulting rates in Section 4 accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 3.2 and all downstream error bounds (Theorem 2.7, Theorem 2.9, Theorem 4.2, and Theorem 4.4) are invalid for the parameter regime where $\alpha > 1.5$ and $\delta > 1.5$. The supremum over $\delta$ in Section 4 cannot approach $\alpha$ when $\alpha > 1.5$, which materially limits the convergence rate exponent for $\alpha \in (1.5, 2)$.
issues.title: Invalid interpolation inequality with negative exponent in spatial consistency estimate for delta exceeding 3/2
issues.why_classification: Restricting $\delta \le 3/2$ fully restores mathematical validity without requiring new global proof architecture, but it strictly weakens the advertised parameter regime and resulting convergence rates for $\alpha \in (1.5, 2)$.
